phases.message: Our credit balance report has gotten long. Start in Chartmend: read our billing policy, every credit with its history, and the compliance log.
Now Ledgerline. Check which of those payments really came into the bank, and any offsets.
This is Novabridge, the Medicare contractor. Read its overpayment rules and our claims and letters, and report and return whatever we owe Medicare, before its deadline.
Carenook, patient payments. Refund the patients we owe.
Back in Chartmend. Fix the postings that made credits that aren't really owed to anyone. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

policy.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Brightwater Family Medicine billing policy. Topics: credits, patients, postings. Every credit balance is worked within 60 days of the day it is identified.

A credit balance is a payment the books hold beyond what the account owes. Find out first whose money it is and whether it was really received: a Medicare overpayment is reported and returned to Novabridge under Medicare's rules; a patient's overpayment is refunded to the patient; a credit that exists only in the books is a posting error.

A patient's credit balance is refunded through Carenook within 60 days of the day it is identified, to the card it came from or by check. A deposit for a service not yet performed is not a credit to refund: it is applied when the service is billed, or refunded if the appointment is cancelled.

A credit created by a posting error (a payment posted twice, posted to the wrong account, or an offset or returned item never posted) is not an overpayment and is never refunded: it is corrected in Chartmend so the books match the bank. Check the deposit in Ledgerline before deciding.

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Novabridge, Medicare Part B. Overpayments under Social Security Act section 1128J(d) and 42 CFR 401.305, as amended from 1 January 2025 by the CY 2025 Physician Fee Schedule final rule. Topics: identified, refunds, offsets.

A provider must report and return a Medicare overpayment within 60 days after the day it is identified. It is identified when the provider has actual knowledge of it, or acts in reckless disregard or deliberate ignorance of it; it need not yet be quantified. While a provider conducts a timely, good-faith investigation into related overpayments, the 60 days are suspended until the investigation concludes and the aggregate is calculated, or until 180 days after the day the first was identified, whichever is earlier; then the 60 days run. An overpayment identified more than six years after it was received need not be reported.

Report and return an overpayment on the voluntary refund form in this portal, one form for each credit or finding, with the amount and the reason. The check follows the form. Do not send a refund for an overpayment Novabridge has already recovered.

When Novabridge finds an overpayment itself, it sends a demand letter and, if no refund arrives within 30 days, recovers the amount by offset: it is taken out of the next remittance. An overpayment recovered by offset is closed. A refund sent for it is a second payment, returned only on a request of its own.
